header.name: Data Structures & Algorithms
header.description: This course is aimed at giving students a background in basic data structures and algorithms along with their impact in solving real life problems using a computer. The major focus will be on covering the basic data structures, b) Algorithm analysis using recurrence relations and c) problem solving using C++.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Students are able to explain, analyze and implement (in C++) basic data structures including but not limited to linked lists, stacks, queues, trees, graphs and dictionaries

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Able to analyze asymptotic complexity of various data structure operations and basic algorithms.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Able to explain, analyze and implement (in C++) basic algorithms like sorting, graph traversals, shortest paths and minimum spanning trees

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Able to effectively compare different data structure and select the appropriate one for efficiently solving a computational problem

weekly_plan.tutorial_assignment: Weekly programming assignments and homeworks to implement and analyse data structures covered in class. Homeworks contain both theoretical and programming problems.

lecture_topics: Sorting Algorithms:- Merge and Quick sort
Tree data structure and Implementations:-binary and complete trees
Graph and Direct Acyclic Graph Algorithms:-BFS, DFS

resources.title: Thomas H. Cormen, Charles E. Leiserson, Ronald L. Rivest, and Clifford Stein: Introduction to Algorithms, MIT press, ISBN 978-0-262-03384-8  (Primary Textbook)
Mark Allan Weiss: Data Structures and Algorithm Analysis in C (Second Edition), Addison-Wesley, 1997
Cormen et al.: Introduction to Algorithms
